statement: The function returns a result r, and r is the maximum total reward in the following exact sense. Let A be the set of all integers s for which there exist an integer k with 0 <= k <= len(rewardValues) and pairwise distinct indices i_0, ..., i_{k-1} in [0, len(rewardValues)) such that, for every t with 0 <= t < k, rewardValues[i_t] > sum_{p=0}^{t-1} rewardValues[i_p], and s = sum_{t=0}^{k-1} rewardValues[i_t]. Then r is an element of A and s <= r for every s in A. Indices are 0-based; the empty choice k = 0 is allowed and has sum 0, and every empty sum above is 0.
preconditions: 1 <= len(rewardValues) <= 50000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(rewardValues), 1 <= rewardValues[i] <= 50000.

statement: For every rewardValues satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail.
preconditions: 1 <= len(rewardValues) <= 50000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(rewardValues), 1 <= rewardValues[i] <= 50000.

statement: The returned value r satisfies r >= max_{0 <= i < len(rewardValues)} rewardValues[i].
preconditions: 1 <= len(rewardValues) <= 50000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(rewardValues), 1 <= rewardValues[i] <= 50000.

statement: Let D be the set of distinct integers that occur as entries of rewardValues, that is, D = { v | there exists i with 0 <= i < len(rewardValues) and rewardValues[i] = v }. Then r <= sum_{v in D} v.
preconditions: 1 <= len(rewardValues) <= 50000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(rewardValues), 1 <= rewardValues[i] <= 50000.

statement: Let M = max_{0 <= i < len(rewardValues)} rewardValues[i]. Then r <= 2*M - 1.
preconditions: 1 <= len(rewardValues) <= 50000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(rewardValues), 1 <= rewardValues[i] <= 50000.
1 <= len(rewardValues) <= 50000, for every i with 0 <= i < len(rewardValues), 1 <= rewardValues[i] <= 50000, and len(rewardValues) = 1.

statement: Let M = max_{0 <= i < len(rewardValues)} rewardValues[i]. Then r = M if and only if for every i with 0 <= i < len(rewardValues), rewardValues[i] = M.
preconditions: 1 <= len(rewardValues) <= 50000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(rewardValues), 1 <= rewardValues[i] <= 50000.

statement: Let M = max_{0 <= i < len(rewardValues)} rewardValues[i], and let L = max{ rewardValues[i] | 0 <= i < len(rewardValues) and rewardValues[i] < M }. Then r >= M + L.
preconditions: 1 <= len(rewardValues) <= 50000, for every i with 0 <= i < len(rewardValues), 1 <= rewardValues[i] <= 50000, and there exists an index i with rewardValues[i] < max_{0 <= j < len(rewardValues)} rewardValues[j].

statement: If r is the result for rewardValues and r' is the result for otherRewards, then r' >= r.
preconditions: rewardValues and otherRewards both satisfy 1 <= len <= 50000 and all their entries lie in [1, 50000], and otherRewards is obtained from rewardValues by inserting one additional entry v with 1 <= v <= 50000, so len(otherRewards) = len(rewardValues) + 1.

statement: If r is the result for rewardValues and r_perm is the result for perm, then r = r_perm.
preconditions: rewardValues and perm both satisfy 1 <= len <= 50000 and all their entries lie in [1, 50000], and perm is a reordering of rewardValues: len(perm) = len(rewardValues) and there is a bijection f from {0, ..., len(rewardValues)-1} to itself such that perm[j] = rewardValues[f(j)] for every j with 0 <= j < len(rewardValues).

statement: If r is the result for rewardValues and r2 is the result for rewardValues2, then r = r2.
preconditions: rewardValues satisfies 1 <= len(rewardValues) <= 50000 and all entries lie in [1, 50000]; there exist distinct indices p and q with rewardValues[p] = rewardValues[q]; rewardValues2 satisfies 1 <= len(rewardValues2) <= 50000 and all entries lie in [1, 50000], and rewardValues2 is obtained from rewardValues by deleting exactly one occurrence of that repeated value, keeping all other entries in their original order.

statement: There exists a subset S of {0, 1, ..., len(rewardValues)-1} such that sum_{i in S} rewardValues[i] = r and, for all i and j in S with i != j, rewardValues[i] != rewardValues[j].
preconditions: 1 <= len(rewardValues) <= 50000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(rewardValues), 1 <= rewardValues[i] <= 50000.

statement: There exist an integer k with 1 <= k <= len(rewardValues) and pairwise distinct indices i_0, ..., i_{k-1} in [0, len(rewardValues)) such that, for every t with 0 <= t < k, rewardValues[i_t] > sum_{p=0}^{t-1} rewardValues[i_p], the total sum_{t=0}^{k-1} rewardValues[i_t] equals r, and, letting v = rewardValues[i_{k-1}] be the last chosen value, 2*v > r.
preconditions: 1 <= len(rewardValues) <= 50000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(rewardValues), 1 <= rewardValues[i] <= 50000.

1 <= len(rewardValues) <= 50000, for every i with 0 <= i < len(rewardValues), 1 <= rewardValues[i] <= 50000; let c_0 < c_1 < ... < c_{m-1} be the distinct values occurring in rewardValues, with m >= 2, and suppose that for every j with 1 <= j < m, c_j > sum_{p=0}^{j-1} c_p.
